This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X Card.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Stocks are tanking.
NASDAQ is now down more than 900 points or more than 3.5%.
The latest earnings reports have investors worried about heavy AI investments.
Here's NPR's Stephen Besaha.
Amazon stock plummeted Thursday after it revealed to investors it spent more than $77 billion
on property and equipment between July and September.
Tech companies are taking on massive debt to pay for data centers to fuel AI.
That's leaving investors with sticker shock and feeling impatient for tangible-proof AI
is worth the price.
Intel stocks also fell sharply after the company revealed disappointing earnings on Thursday
and that the chip-making business is straining under high manufacturing costs and demand.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
In Alaska's close U.S. Senate race, Democrat Mary Pultola is forcefully denying an allegation
in a New York Times story that NPR has not independently confirmed.
Alaska Public Media's Liz Ruskin says the report claims Pultola knew of a project to
recruit a spoiler candidate named Dan Sullivan to help her unseat the Republican incumbent
also named Dan Sullivan.
The Democratic former congresswoman spoke to supporters in Juneau Thursday night.
I knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent.
That is all I have ever known about.
I am not interested in tricking voters.
Republicans, including President Trump, have complained for months that the second Sullivan
is intended to confuse Alaskans and draw votes away from the Senator.
Trump has called for Pultola to be removed from the race and charged with a crime, though
it's not clear what law would apply.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
Various cities and states have reported a spike in ICE activity ahead of Tuesday's midterm
elections.
More from NPR's Jasmine Garz.
Recently, there have been reports of a surge in ICE arrests in Illinois, Oregon, Detroit,
California, and New York City.
In a statement to NPR, DHS wrote, "ICE agents uphold our nation's immigration laws in all
50 states seven days a week."
Wendy Weiser with the Brennan Center for Justice at NYU says voter participation remains strong.
Americans are tuning this out and we are not seeing a significant impact on participation.
And we're actually seeing huge surges in participation in communities of color and in Latino communities.
And even though it hasn't happened, she reminds people that intimidation at the polls is illegal.
Jasmine Garz and PR News, New York.
Krista Pike speaking out for the first time since her botched execution for murder in
Tennessee.
In a statement released today, a month after surviving two lethal injections of pentobarbital,
Pike says she feels pain in her body, mind, and soul.
Americans are on hold for now in Tennessee pending a review.
This is NPR News.
Colorectal cancer has become the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among people under
the age of 50.
From member station GBH, Mark Hurst reports on a new study.
Dr. Anna Anderson is an immunologist and cancer researcher at the Brigham and Women's Hospital
in Boston.
She and others found that younger people have more stromal cells, a sort of connective tissue
cell, in their tumors, which is not good.
Tumors that are rich in stromal cells are resistant to chemotherapy.
Those same cells also suppress the immune system of the patient from being able to kill
the tumor cells.
The study also found a certain kind of cell change in younger people's cancers that made
their tumors more aggressive and, it found, a previously unstudied group of genes in those
people whose role has yet to be uncovered.
For NPR News, I'm Mark Hurst in Boston.
The Star Trek universe is mourning two major cast losses this week.
Sir Patrick Stewart, who played Captain Jean-Luc Picard, died yesterday at the age of 86 and
Walter Koenig, who played Ensign Pavel Chekhov, died Sunday.
He lived 90 years.
Fans had showered love on the 2026 World Series Champions from the sidelines of a parade in
Milwaukee and online today.
Fans across the U.S. were celebrating the Brewers' first franchise title.
They defeated the Tampa Bay Rays Wednesday four games to one.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

Krista Pike speaks publicly for first time since botched Tennessee execution

Actors Patrick Stewart and Walter Koenig, of Star Trek fame, die within days of each other
Milwaukee Brewers win first franchise World Series title, defeating Tampa Bay Rays four games to one
